layers.name: Formal representation
layers.plain: How claims, world models and data are written down so a machine can check them.

model.text: Notation: latent quantities Θ, world model M = (G, p), evidence, named assumptions
Correspondence to the Alloy-checked formal core
Data as sets of addressable facts that methods transform

worked.text: The formal representation layer, kept apart from the other seven
worked.note: Not cited. The agent model has its own formal core, which fits this layer but was never checked against it.

worked.text: Use MMT-style formal artifacts; a rough draft candidate is a different thing from a formal artifact
worked.note: Not cited. Section 12's rival world models start as drafts, so this distinction applies there.

worked.text: A guarantee carries across a change of representation only through a certified preservation relation; otherwise re-warrant
worked.note: Section 11 receipts say a fact was preserved or approximated, but never whether its warrant survives the step. Decision 018 is the rule for that.

layers.name: Candidate generation
layers.plain: Where candidate explanations, hypotheses and world models come from, before anyone judges them.

model.text: One sentence: candidates may come from any generator, and the generator confers no warrant (planned, no code)
Candidate methods come from the workbench's router

worked.text: Draft state, construction operators, strategy, formal elaboration, evaluation and feedback, warrant kept separate; a worked trace from the founding dialogue (§10)
worked.note: Section 12 cites only §1 and §7. Operators, strategy, evaluation feedback, the general loop and Frames (§15) are not used.

worked.text: Candidate generation is a typed generative system; exploring inside it is different from changing the system itself
worked.note: Not used. Adding a new kind of world model (a new causal-discovery method, say) is a change to the system, not a step inside it.

worked.text: The interface survives mapping onto CEGIS, meta-interpretive learning, anti-unification, HR and conceptual blending
worked.note: Not used. It is evidence that the interface can host the generators section 12 names.

worked.text: Combine generators with a blackboard, an explicit controller, a generator portfolio and reflection; invent no new glue calculus
worked.note: Not used. Section 12 lists several generators (causal discovery, an analyst, an LLM) with no way to combine them. Decision 017 is that way.

worked.text: Prior-art reviews behind 015–017 (adapters, provenance across generators, portfolio growth)
worked.note: Not cited.

layers.name: Support
layers.plain: What backs a claim and how strongly: which evidence and assumptions it rests on.

model.text: Belief as a posterior; a claim's credence
Lineage through receipts: which input facts a result came from, and what an audit reaches

worked.text: ATMS-style support labels: the sets of assumptions a claim rests on, with rules for alternative and joint support
worked.note: Not used. Section 11's 'reach' answers the same question (which conclusions depend on this input) with a separate mechanism.

worked.text: Persistent support and temporary contexts, the positive support algebra, graded support
worked.note: Not cited.

worked.text: Record where support came from before grading it; provenance semirings; why adding up numeric support naively is unsafe
worked.note: Not cited. Provenance semirings are the established prior art for section 11's lineage.

worked.text: A numeric support score warrants reporting a grade, not accepting the claim; acting needs its own warrant rule
worked.note: The agent model's own 'stakes bar' rule accepts a claim whenever its probability clears a bar. Decision 010 says a probability alone does not warrant accepting. Someone has to decide which one holds.

layers.name: Argument / defeat
layers.plain: What attacks a claim, and whether the claim survives the attack.

model.text: An audit withdraws licences by removing an assumption (for example, 'the source is reliable')
R-619 challenge closure: what a challenge reaches
A belief state lists rival claims with their credences

worked.text: Licences that needed a withdrawn assumption are withdrawn by name
worked.note: Used through licence.py (decision 036).

worked.text: Assumption-based argumentation: assumptions with contraries, attacks, and whether an argument survives explicit defeat
worked.note: Not used. Rival claims in section 1 are never set against each other as attacks; they only carry credences.

worked.text: How arguments are identified; preferences between them; refuse to decide when preference meaning is incomplete
worked.note: Not cited.

layers.name: Warrant
layers.plain: Whether the backing is good enough, judged under a named standard.

model.text: Who judges each condition: computed, AI or human
Four rules of its own in licence.py: stakes bar, deterministic check, source label, conjunction
A model revision names its warrant (planned)

worked.text: Every judgment names its standard, assumptions and certificate
worked.note: Used: licence.py builds WarrantJudgments.

worked.text: Pick a strategy only when the lower confidence bound on its paired advantage is above zero
worked.note: Used for the act-on-network policy.

worked.text: Deductive warrant is a checked derivation from explicit premises; the premises are not thereby accepted
worked.note: Rebuilt locally as 'o2a.deterministic-check/1'.

worked.text: Measurement and testimony warrant recording a result relative to a model, not accepting the proposition
worked.note: Rebuilt locally as 'o2a.source-label/1'. The 'stakes bar' rule also turns a model-relative posterior into acceptance; 012 says the posterior regime 'does not warrant accepting the claim'.

worked.text: Statistical warrant from finite-class uniform-convergence bounds under explicit sampling assumptions
worked.note: Not used.

worked.text: Grounded dialectical warrant; what warrants a warrant rule itself (§13)
worked.note: Not cited.

layers.name: Licence
layers.plain: What the agent may do with a claim in a given use: state it, build on it, act on it.

model.text: Condition statuses and standing; the acceptance policies 'describe-findings' and 'act-on-network'; accepting is not acting

worked.text: A licence is derived only when the warrant fits the action and its assumptions hold
worked.note: Used: decision 036 hands licence to epistemic-warrant, pinned at b891812e.

worked.text: Acceptance is a context-relative action governed by an explicit policy over typed warrant obligations
worked.note: Used in effect: the two acceptance policies name a context and the warrant rules they accept.

worked.text: Combining licences is different from choosing an action
worked.note: Matches 'accepting is not acting'; not cited.

layers.name: Epistemic action / update
layers.plain: How the agent's state of belief changes, including adding or dropping whole hypotheses.

model.text: Bayesian update on a new observation; which claims an observation reaches
Predictions recorded and scored when outcomes arrive
Record of past cases
A falsified world model is removed or down-weighted (planned)

worked.text: Changing the hypothesis universe: adding or removing hypotheses is a different kind of change from updating credences over a fixed set
worked.note: Not cited. This is exactly what section 12 does when it adds or removes world models.

worked.text: Reading out a result is not necessarily a change of state; candidate generation, warrant and update stay separate
worked.note: Not cited.

worked.text: An epistemic action is a partial transducer with preconditions and an effect footprint; no fixed taxonomy of actions
worked.note: Not cited.

layers.name: Strategy / control
layers.plain: How the agent decides what to think about, what to run and when to stop.

model.text: Decision by expected utility
When to think harder: value of a deliberation against its cost
Oversight policy and gates anywhere
Attention: priority by expected value of information
Method advice ordered by track record

worked.text: Paired performance certificates for choosing a strategy
worked.note: Used for act-on-network. Section 9 orders methods by mean usefulness instead, without the lower-bound rule. That is a smaller gap.

worked.text: Operators, strategies, strategy episodes; checks of a factorization (complete, minimal, independent, compositional, unique); under-, over- and misfactored diagnostics; strategy versus metastrategy; reflection; monitoring and control
worked.note: Not cited. Sections 4 and 7 are monitoring and control in this sense.

worked.text: An explicit controller over a portfolio of knowledge sources
worked.note: Not used.

worked.text: Prior-art check of the eight-layer factorization itself
worked.note: Not cited.
